newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar emir home after making up with ousted father.
newsitem.headline: Qatar emir home after making up with ousted father.

text.p: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani returned home from Europe on Wednesday after making peace with the father he ousted in a palace coup.
The official Qatari news agency said the emir brought back with him his uncle, Sheikh Mohammad bin Hamad al-Thani, who was in self-exile with his ousted brother.
The agency did not give further details.

The emir and his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, agreed at a meeting in Paris last week "to end family differences between them and start a new page of family ties based on love and mutual respect and appreciation."
The agreement did not say when the former emir, toppled in 1995, would return home.
But officials in Doha said Sheikh Khalifa, 66, is expected to return soon after the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, due to start later this week.

"Though he will not hold any position in the government, except for a top status in the order of protocol, he will still remain a central figure in our society, as elder statesman and father of the emir," said an official close to the emiri diwan (royal court).
Also returning home with the former emir will be his close advisors, including his former office director Issa Ghanem al-Kuwari and former education minister
The rest of his 200 associates, who had left Qatar after his ouster, will follow later, they added.
Qatar had accused the emir's followers of being behind a foiled coup attempt last year. The former emir had denied any involvement.
Diplomats said the reconciliation between father and son had removed a major source of concern for the Emir Sheikh Hamad.
"Though he has already settled himself in the saddle, the ousted emir had remained a source of concern for him," an Arab diplomat said.

The former emir remains a "popular figure" in Qatar, said a western diplomat. "He is regarded as helmsman of Qatar's prosperity during the transition from the pearl trade to oil era and commands unmatched loyalty, especially among the older people".
"The reconciliation was the best thing to have happened at a time when Qatar is seeking billions of dollars in foreign investment to develop its gas reserves," he added.

Qatar, a small oil producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), sits on the world's third largest reserves of natural gas and has embarked on a number of projects to transform it into cash.
